allowed_input_index_digest.canonicalization: UTF-8 of ordered newline-separated path@github_blob_sha entries

memory_leads.memory: A ship's exit from trading commonly involves an owner decision, sale negotiation, an intermediary or cash buyer, delivery under agreed conditions, a final voyage or tow, transfer to a recycling yard, cutting and downstream sale of recovered steel/equipment. The contractual buyer and the physical demolition yard can be different actors.
memory_leads.why_useful: Turns scrapping from a fleet statistic into an auditable transaction trajectory.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Exact title-transfer terms, buyer identity and jurisdiction-specific obligations require Evidence.

memory_leads.memory: Cash buyers are remembered as a distinctive intermediary class that can buy vessels from owners and resell or deliver them to recycling yards, bridging owner credit/reputation constraints and yard financing or market access.
memory_leads.why_useful: Adds a hidden commercial layer between shipowner and demolition yard.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Do not generalize financing, title or agency relationships across firms or periods.

memory_leads.memory: End-of-life sales can be structured around delivery at a named place or on an as-is basis, leaving meaningful final-voyage, bunkers, seaworthiness, insurance and delay risk between trading exit and physical demolition.
memory_leads.why_useful: Explains why fleet exit is not instantaneous when a demolition sale is agreed.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Exact sale-form wording and responsibility allocation are Evidence-first.

memory_leads.memory: Strong discovery anchors include South Asian beaching-yard clusters such as Alang, Chattogram/Chittagong and Gadani, and Turkish yards around Aliaga; other countries and historical periods used different facilities and methods. Beaching, landing, alongside and dry-dock-like methods create different infrastructure and containment questions.
memory_leads.why_useful: Adds a physical end-of-life geography without ranking current yards.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Current market shares, active-yard lists and method classifications require source verification.

memory_leads.memory: Demolition economics are often discussed using lightweight displacement or similar recoverable-weight measures and a price per unit of lightweight, because steel and recoverable material value rather than cargo deadweight drives the buyer's salvage value.
memory_leads.why_useful: Adds a distinct end-of-life valuation semantic that should not be confused with DWT or vessel market value.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Exact definitions, deductions and regional price quotations require Evidence.

memory_leads.memory: The decision to recycle can compare continued earning optionality against scrap value, expected freight recovery, secondhand value, fuel efficiency, upcoming repair/class-survey cost, regulatory retrofit cost and financing burden. A weak freight market does not mechanically imply demolition if owners retain recovery expectations.
memory_leads.why_useful: Makes scrapping a Judgment/option-value decision rather than a deterministic age threshold.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: No universal age, survey interval or trigger is asserted.

memory_leads.memory: Large dry-docking, special-survey or life-extension expenditures are remembered as common decision points for older vessels: an owner may compare the next certification/repair package with residual earning prospects and demolition value.
memory_leads.why_useful: Refines atlas scrapping optionality with a concrete maintenance-capex decision point.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Survey cycles and class requirements vary and exact rules require Evidence.

memory_leads.memory: Ship recycling research repeatedly encounters asbestos, PCBs, ozone-depleting substances, oils/sludges, paints/heavy metals and other hazardous materials, plus the concept of an Inventory of Hazardous Materials or similar onboard inventory before recycling.
memory_leads.why_useful: Creates source-discovery vocabulary linking ship design/maintenance history to end-of-life handling.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Exact regulated substances, thresholds and document requirements depend on regime and vintage.

memory_leads.memory: Recycling hazards remembered at mechanism level include hot-work fire/explosion, gas-freeing failures, confined spaces, falling steel/structures, lifting operations and exposure to hazardous substances. Safe dismantling therefore depends on sequencing and preparation, not only yard location.
memory_leads.why_useful: Adds worker-safety mechanisms to a topic often reduced to scrap tonnage.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Specific accidents or compliance findings require Evidence.

memory_leads.memory: A recycling yard's environmental performance depends on containment of oils, residues, paint chips and hazardous waste, drainage/soil/water controls, and where recovered or hazardous material goes downstream after cutting. Yard-gate compliance alone may not describe the full waste chain.
memory_leads.why_useful: Extends provenance thinking from the vessel to downstream material handling.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Do not infer facility performance without source-grounded inspections or records.

memory_leads.memory: The Basel Convention/waste-shipment framework, the Hong Kong ship-recycling convention framework and the EU ship-recycling regime are strong remembered source-discovery anchors for end-of-life controls, alongside flag, port, owner and recycling-state rules.
memory_leads.why_useful: Creates an Evidence task vocabulary while keeping legal chronology out of blind recall.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Exact entry-into-force dates, scope, flag applicability, waste classification and legal interactions must be verified from authoritative texts.

memory_leads.memory: Industry discussion remembers last-voyage changes of flag, ownership or corporate vehicle around recycling transactions. These can affect which regulator, financier or counterparty sees the vessel at end of life, but motives and legality are case-specific.
memory_leads.why_useful: Adds an identity/revision trail to end-of-life research rather than assuming continuous ownership and flag.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Do not label a specific flag or transaction evasive without claim-scoped Evidence.

memory_leads.memory: Cash buyers and yards can face substantial working-capital exposure between buying the vessel and monetizing recovered steel and equipment. Scrap-price movements, currency/credit conditions and payment security can therefore influence transaction timing and counterparty selection.
memory_leads.why_useful: Connects end-of-life capacity to credit conditions rather than treating scrap buyers as cash-neutral.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Exact financing instruments and margins vary by market and firm.

memory_leads.memory: Higher recoverable-steel values can raise the floor under demolition bids, while weak shipping earnings reduce the value of keeping old tonnage trading. The interaction can accelerate fleet removal and affect how quickly oversupply clears.
memory_leads.why_useful: Refines the atlas capital-cycle/scrapping link with the recycling-side demand signal.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: No exact elasticity or cycle chronology is claimed.

memory_leads.memory: When many vessels seek exit at once, suitable yard capacity, beach/berth space, labor, local steel absorption, financing and regulatory acceptance can constrain the pace of demolition. Announced scrapping therefore need not translate immediately into removed effective supply.
memory_leads.why_useful: Adds a lag and capacity constraint to fleet-exit modeling.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Current yard capacity and regional bottlenecks require source-first research.

memory_leads.memory: Older hulls may sometimes compete between continued trading, conversion/redeployment and demolition. Offshore or storage conversions are remembered examples of alternative terminal paths, so final fleet exit should preserve the chosen trajectory rather than treating every sale of an old vessel as scrap.
memory_leads.why_useful: Links P004 conversion topology to end-of-life option value without merging the two states.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Specific conversion economics and project histories require Evidence.

memory_leads.memory: Beyond formal law, cargo owners, lenders, insurers, investors and large shipowners can impose recycling policies, yard-audit expectations or responsible-recycling commitments that influence which yards are commercially acceptable.
memory_leads.why_useful: Adds non-state governance to end-of-life decisions.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Specific policy names, adoption dates and contractual force require Evidence.

memory_leads.memory: Scrapping is a supply-side adjustment margin whose timing depends on vessel age, debt, expected recovery and scrap value.
memory_leads.why_useful: Confirms the atlas mechanism but adds little novelty alone.
memory_leads.precision_caveat: Already present in the compact atlas.

memory_leads.memory: Downturns can force deleveraging and transfer or retirement of vessels as capital providers reassess asset values.
memory_leads.why_useful: Connects recycling to the existing capital-cycle atlas theme.

method_observation.observation: End-of-life probing remains high-yield when 'scrapped' is decomposed into decision, sale, intermediary, final voyage, yard acceptance, dismantling and downstream material handling. A terminal-state label hides time lags, identity changes, credit and safety constraints; future trajectory probes should unpack terminal states into transitions before enumerating actors.

stop_reason: The preset questions were answered with a coherent end-of-life transaction and constraint topology. Marginal recall then shifted toward exact buyer lineages, yard rankings/compliance, legal applicability and sale-form liability; those require claim-scoped Evidence or would become country/company catalog work.
